title: Drying, inspection and handover
audience: Carpet and upholstery cleaners who dry, inspect and hand over the cleaned item.
referencesAtStart: Official sources: ACCC, False or misleading claims (no date in the body; page metadata shows 28 June 2026).
learningOutcomes: Dry the item fully using airflow and the approved method, and confirm dryness before release.
Inspect the cleaned item against the agreed scope and record any limits that remain.
Hand over without promising a result beyond the inspection.

instruction.heading: Drying properly before release
instruction.body: Drying is part of the cleaning, not an afterthought. Moisture moves into the lowest and thickest parts of an item, which means the backing, the edges, the seams and the underside of an upholstered cushion are the places that stay damp longest. The surface can feel dry while the layers below remain wet, and that hidden dampness is where odour and growth start. Use airflow across the item, such as fans or air movers placed according to the equipment maker's instructions, and keep traffic and furniture off the item until it is dry. Check the backing, the edges and the seams by touch and, where the business has an approved moisture check, by reading. Record the time the drying started, the checks made and the time the item was confirmed dry. Where an item stays wet well beyond the time the method and the conditions would normally allow, stop and find out why before release.

instruction.heading: Inspecting against the agreed scope
instruction.body: Inspect the cleaned item against the scope and limits signed before the work. Work from several angles and in good light, and compare the item with the pre-work photographs and the record. Record the stains that remain, any change in colour or texture, any residue or tide marks, any change in pile direction or pile height, and any damage. Separate what the cleaning achieved from what it did not achieve. A short, factual record is more useful than a general statement that the item looks good, because the record is what the customer and the business rely on if the result is questioned.

instruction.heading: Dampness, odour and suspected growth
instruction.body: Persistent dampness can lead to odour and to growth, which are outside routine cleaning. If the item smells musty after drying, if a damp area remains at the backing after the expected time, or if any growth is visible, do not release the item as complete. Keep the item out of use, record the location and the observations with photographs taken with permission, and refer it to a qualified service. Do not treat a damp item as dry because the customer wants it back.

instruction.heading: Stains that can return
instruction.body: Some soils and stains can wick back up as the item dries and is used, and a residue left behind can attract new soil. The customer should understand this before the handover, because a stain that looks removed can reappear after use. Explain the likely behaviour in plain terms, and record that it was explained. Do not describe any stain as permanently removed unless the inspection and the test support that statement, and even then, describe it as the result seen on the day.

instruction.heading: Handover with the record
instruction.body: Hand over with the written record: the scope that was done, the method used, the drying check, the remaining limits, any items referred, and the follow-up the business offers. Explain the result plainly, and show the customer the areas where the result is limited. Agree any further work separately, with its own scope and price. Give the customer any maintenance advice the product label or the maker gives. Any statement about the result needs a reasonable basis at the time it is made, and the business must be able to show that basis if asked (ACCC, False or misleading claims, fetched 2026-11-03). Obtain the customer's signature on the handover record.

instruction.heading: After the handover
instruction.body: Keep the handover record with the job file. If the customer reports a change after the handover, compare the report with the pre-work record, the inspection record and the drying record, and respond with the evidence. Do not change the record after the event; add a dated note instead, and keep both.

procedure: Dry the item fully with airflow, and keep traffic and furniture off until it is dry.
Check the backing, edges and seams by touch, and by reading where the business approves a moisture check.
If the item stays damp beyond the expected time, or smells musty, stop, record it, and refer it to a qualified service before release.
Inspect against the agreed scope from several angles, in good light, and compare with the pre-work record.
Record the remaining stains, colour or texture change, residue, pile change and damage, and separate what was achieved from what was not.
Explain the likely return of some stains, and hand over with the written record, the limits and the follow-up.
Obtain the customer's signature on the handover record, and file it with the job record.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaned carpet feels dry on top, but the edges and the seams are still damp to the touch.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do before release?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not release the carpet. Keep airflow on the edges and seams, keep traffic and furniture off, and recheck the backing until it is dry. Record the drying checks and the times, and the reason the release was held. Release only when the backing, edges and seams are confirmed dry by the method the business has approved, and record the confirmation.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A fabric upholstered cushion feels dry on the face, but the seam at the back is still damp and a faint musty smell is noticed after the fans have been running for a while.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you hand the cushion back, and what do you record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not hand the cushion back as complete. Keep it out of use, record the seam, the smell and the time with photographs taken with permission, and refer the item to a qualified service because the damp and the smell are outside routine cleaning. Tell the customer the reason in plain terms, and record the referral. Do not describe the item as complete until the referral has been answered and the local requirement has been checked.

workedExamples.situation: (Example job) A customer asks you to guarantee in writing that a stain you have treated will never return.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you write on the handover record?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not write the guarantee. Record the result seen on the day, the limits that remain, and the likelihood that some stains can wick back up as the item dries and is used. Explain that the statement is based on the inspection at handover, and offer a follow-up inspection as a separate job if the customer wants one. Keep the basis for the description in the job file, because the ACCC guidance expects a business to be able to show the basis for a statement about a result.

equipmentAndPpe: Air movers or fans, placed according to the equipment maker's instructions
Moisture check method approved by the business, with its reading recorded
Torch and magnifier for the final inspection in good light
Camera or phone for handover photographs, used with the customer's permission
Handover record form for the scope, method, drying check, limits and signature
Gloves when checking damp or possibly soiled areas

commonErrors.error: Releasing a carpet that feels dry only on top.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the backing, edges and seams, and record the drying check and the time.

commonErrors.error: Promising a stain will never return.
commonErrors.prevention: Explain that some stains can wick back up, and record the explanation.

commonErrors.error: Calling the job perfect without an inspection and a record.
commonErrors.prevention: Inspect against the scope from several angles, and record the result and the limits.

commonErrors.error: Handing back a damp item because the customer wants it back.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold the release until the item is confirmed dry, and refer any odour or growth.

commonErrors.error: Editing a handover record after a complaint without a dated note.
commonErrors.prevention: Add a dated note and keep the original record unchanged.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Persistent dampness can lead to odour and growth, which are outside routine cleaning.
Statements about a result must have a reasonable basis at the time they are made, and the business must be able to show that basis (ACCC, False or misleading claims).
No Australian standard for drying carpet or upholstery was confirmed for this lesson.
The content needs subject-matter and regulator review before use.

qualityStandard: Drying is confirmed at the backing, edges and seams before release, in the practical.
The inspection record shows the remaining limits and separates what was achieved from what was not, in the simulated job.
The handover is made with the record and without a guarantee that a stain will not return, in the simulated job.
A damp item, or one with odour or growth, is held and referred rather than released, in the case study.
documentationEvidence: Drying check record with the start time, the checks made and the confirmed dry time
Inspection record with the remaining limits, separate from the achieved result
Referral record for any odour, damp or growth
Handover record with the scope, method, limits, follow-up and the customer's signature
summary: Dry fully, including the backing, edges and seams, before release.
Inspect against the agreed scope and record the limits that remain.
Explain the likely return of some stains, and do not guarantee the result.
Hold and refer any damp item that smells or shows growth.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked before release?
options: The colour of the carpet only, nothing else
That the backing, edges and seams are dry
The price of the job and the invoice total

knowledgeChecks.question: A customer asks whether a stain will ever return. What is correct?
options: Promise that it will never return, since the clean removed it fully
Explain that some stains can wick back up, and do not guarantee the result
Say that it always returns, so the customer should expect it again

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is incomplete drying a concern?
options: It can lead to odour and growth, which are outside routine cleaning
It makes the item stiff and uncomfortable for the owner to use
It is not a concern once the surface looks dry to the eye

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a statement about the result have when it is made?
options: Only the customer's hope that the result will last for years to come after the clean
A reasonable basis at the time it is made, which the business must be able to show
Nothing, if the customer signs the handover record at the end of the job
